title: Integral local systems and their normalized reduction towers
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the continuous-function coefficient sheaves $A_X$ and $E_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients], and write $A_{n,X}$ for the constant sheaf of the finite ring $A/\varpi^nA$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There are canonical ring-sheaf isomorphisms $A_X\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A_{n,X}$, $A_X/\varpi^nA_X\cong A_{n,X}$ and $A_X[1/\ell]\cong E_X$, compatible with the reduction and inclusion maps. Limits are limits of sheaves, and localization is the sheaf colimit of repeated multiplication by $\ell$.

For a ring sheaf $R$ let $\operatorname{Loc}(R)$ be the full category of sheaf $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] locally isomorphic, for a pro-etale covering, to a finite direct sum of copies of $R$, allowing rank zero and locally varying ranks. Let $\mathcal T_X(A)$ have objects towers $(F_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$ with $F_n\in\operatorname{Loc}(A_{n,X})$ and $A_{n,X}\otimes_{A_{n+1,X}}F_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n$ induced by $t_n$, where tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Morphisms are compatible families of module maps. Then reduction is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Loc}(A_X)\longrightarrow\mathcal T_X(A),\qquad M\longmapsto(M/\varpi^nM)_n.$$
A quasi-inverse is $(F_n)_n\longmapsto\varprojlim_nF_n$, with its induced $A_X$-action. The natural maps $M\to\varprojlim_nM/\varpi^nM$ and $(\varprojlim_nF_n)/\varpi^n\to F_n$ are isomorphisms, naturally in modules and towers.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; the reduction ring identification is the rank-one reduction in this proposition.

proof.text: Identify the finite constant sheaf $A_{n,X}$ with $V\mapsto C(|V|,A/\varpi^n)$: the finite-set clause of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] represents it by the disjoint union of copies of X, and a map to that disjoint union is exactly its clopen fibre partition. Completeness in [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](2), applied to the finite A-module A, gives $A=\varprojlim A/\varpi^n$. The DVR and absolute-value conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] show that its congruence cosets form an open neighbourhood basis: for $r=|\varpi|<1$, $\varpi^n A=\{a:|a|\leq r^n\}$, these balls are open by the ultrametric inequality, and $r^n\to0$. Thus compatible continuous residue functions give a unique continuous A-valued function, pointwise, and conversely. Limits of module sheaves are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). This proves the ring limit identification, including its projections and restrictions.

Reduction of continuous functions modulo $\varpi^n$ is surjective even on sections: choose a lift in A for each of the finitely many residue values and compose the residue function with this finite discrete section. Its kernel consists exactly of $\varpi^n$ times continuous A-valued functions, since division by $\varpi^n$ is continuous on $\varpi^n A$. Hence $A_X/\varpi^n A_X\cong A_{n,X}$. For localization, each continuous $f:|V|\to E$ has the Zariski open covering $f^{-1}(\ell^{-m}A)$, $m\geq0$. These sets cover since $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}<1$; each is open since A is open. On the m-th member, $f=\ell^{-m}(\ell^mf)$ with $\ell^mf$ A-valued. The resulting fraction map from the sheaf colimit of multiplication by $\ell$ to $E_X$ is epic; it is monic because A embeds in E and multiplication by $\ell$ is injective on A-valued functions. The sheafification-of-sectionwise-colimit description in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2) justifies checking this locally on fractions. Ring operations and the inclusion and reduction maps are the stated pointwise ones.

For a lisse $A_X$-module M restrict to a pro-etale covering on which $M=A_X^r$, with r finite on each member. Slice restriction is evaluation on the same objects, with the same coverings [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; sectionwise limits and sheafified sectionwise quotients therefore commute with restriction. Step 2 gives $M/\varpi^nM=A_{n,X}^r$ there, so its reductions are in the stated category and the normalization map is an isomorphism. Step 1 gives $M\to\varprojlim_n M/\varpi^nM$ an isomorphism on that covering, hence globally: its inverse maps on the cover agree on overlaps since they invert the same map. These calculations include r=0 and require no bound on the ranks over different covering members.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1): full faithfulness and the unit (the source leaves the proof to the reader)

proof.text: Now start with a normalized tower $(F_n,t_n)$. Each $t_n$ is an epimorphism: by the sheafification definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], locally a section of the sheaf tensor quotient is a finite sum of elementary tensors, and lifting its coefficients through the surjection $A_{n+1,X}\to A_{n,X}$ shows that quotient map $F_{n+1}\to A_{n,X}\otimes F_{n+1}$ is epic. Choose a cover trivializing $F_1$ with rank r, then refine it by [det-pe-wcb-cover] to objects $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with D w-contractible. Exactness of sections of abelian sheaves on such U, [det-pe-wc-sections-exact], makes each $F_{n+1}(U)\to F_n(U)$ surjective (module epimorphisms are underlying abelian epimorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1)). Choose the r basis sections of $F_1|_U$ and lift them recursively to r sections at every level, compatibly with $t_n$. The lifts define compatible maps $b_n:A_{n,X}^r|_U\to F_n|_U$. We claim by induction that every $b_n$ is invertible. The base n=1 is the chosen basis. For the induction step, trivialize $F_{n+1}$ on a further cover. Its reduction is $F_n$, so the reduction of $b_{n+1}$ is invertible. On a nonempty trivializing object V, write the matrix of $b_{n+1}$ as B, with s rows and r columns. Its reduction modulo $\varpi^n$ has an inverse matrix of sections. Reducing both matrix identities further modulo $\varpi$ and evaluating their continuous-function entries at any $x\in |V|$ gives inverse linear maps between $k^r$ and $k^s$, where $k=A/\varpi A$; hence s=r. If V is empty the map is already an isomorphism. Lift each entry of the inverse matrix from $A_{n,X}(V)$ to $A_{n+1,X}(V)$ by composing with a choice of representatives of the finite quotient, as in step 2; call the lifted matrix C. Both $BC-1=N$ and $CB-1=P$ have entries in $I=\varpi^n A_{n+1,X}(V)$, whose square is zero since $2n\geq n+1$. Thus $B\,C(1-N)=1$ and $(1-P)C\,B=1$. A left and a right inverse agree, since $L=L(BR)=(LB)R=R$, so B is invertible. This proves the claim, locally and then by gluing inverses. No simultaneous trivialization of the countable tower has been assumed; the recursively lifted bases construct one.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1): omitted compatible-basis argument, using the weakly contractible basis of §4.2

proof.text: Regard every $F_n$ as an $A_X$-module through $A_X\to A_{n,X}$; the $t_n$ are then $A_X$-linear. Define $F=\varprojlim_n F_n$ sectionwise, with the componentwise action of $A_X=\varprojlim A_{n,X}$, as permitted by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). On each U from step 4 the compatible bases give $F|_U=\varprojlim A_{n,X}^r|_U=A_X^r|_U$, since r is finite and a compatible tuple is precisely r compatible coordinate sequences. The defining projections become the usual coordinate reductions there. Consequently they induce $F/\varpi^nF\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n$, respecting the transition maps. Slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] preserves these limits and quotients by the sectionwise description. Thus F is lisse globally and the displayed isomorphisms are canonical: they are induced by the global projections, so their locally computed inverses agree on overlaps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1): effectivity of the compatible tower

proof.text: For a compatible family of tower morphisms $(f_n)$ define the map on limits by $(x_n)\mapsto(f_nx_n)$. This is $A_X$-linear and functorial. The unit $M\to\varprojlim M/\varpi^nM$ of step 3 commutes with a module map because both composites have n-th coordinate its reduction. The counit $(\varprojlim F_n)/\varpi^n\to F_n$ of step 5 commutes with a tower map by the same coordinate formula. Both are isomorphisms, so these two functors are quasi-inverse, proving the asserted equivalence and all naturality clauses. In particular a module map is recovered uniquely from its reductions, by the unit isomorphism and the fact that projections determine a limit map. For an empty base the zero sheaf and empty covering give the same formulas.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.4(1), pp. 58–59. The proposition says its proof is left to the reader; steps 3–6 supply it using the weakly contractible basis.

STATEMENT: it matches Prop. 6.8.4(1) with the coefficient identities of Lemma 6.8.2, for any scheme X and finite E. The towers are normalized as the 2-limit requires, and nothing is weakened. STEPS: (1) the constant sheaf of A/ϖ^n is identified with continuous functions through finite-set representability; A ≅ lim A/ϖ^n holds as topological rings by the ultrametric balls; limits are sectionwise. (2) The kernel of reduction is ϖ^n times continuous functions, and localization at ℓ is checked locally on the Zariski cover f^{-1}(ℓ^{-m}A); this is elementary as marked. (3) Restriction to a slice commutes with limits, quotients and tensors, so the unit is an isomorphism locally and hence globally. (4) Each t_n is epic. Basis sections lift level by level on w-contractible U (det-pe-wcb-cover, det-pe-wc-sections-exact). In the induction, N=BC−1 and P=CB−1 lie in an ideal of square zero because 2n≥n+1, so B has a left and a right inverse; this works for rectangular matrices too. (5) The limit is computed in the compatible bases, giving A_X^r locally and the counit isomorphism. (6) Naturality is checked coordinatewise. EDGE CASES: empty X, non-quasi-compact X, r=0, varying ranks, n=1, A=Z_ℓ, residue characteristic equal to ℓ. One implicit step: the spectral-norm topology equals the |·|_E topology by the uniqueness clause of lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value; this is one line and accepted. There are no new nodes. Duplicate search found no node stating this equivalence; sk-lem-integral-models is a derived Noetherian statement, not this one.
